  `tmp/d145/vol145.py`; genus, components and watertightness per frame from the meshes JSON; training and
  reconstruction wall-clock per pair. *Expected (Buonomo et al.'s Fig. 10, 12 and Tab. 9).* NISE is faster than their
  method (0.17–0.6 × its time; about 10–30 min a pair here). It has no volume constraint, and its intermediate
  volume varies far more than BUO's, with blobby intermediates and parts that can vanish. The end is near BUO's
  (silhouette IoU about 0.90–0.96). Results are recorded as found.
  **B13, the control variable: an external force in place of the stress control (pre-registered 2026-10-15 12:08 CDT
  server clock, before any measured run; the B13 agent on the coordinator's brief; branch `wip/b13` from refreeze-prep
  2b0cafc; `tmp/b13/`, `output/gpu/b13/`; a baseline mode that changes nothing of ours).** Classical physics-based shape
  control drives the body toward the target with external forces (Treuille et al. 2003; McNamara et al. 2004; Fattal and
  Lischinski 2004; Chen, Levin and Langlois, SIGGRAPH 2024; Li et al., SIGGRAPH Asia 2025). A reviewer will ask why we
  control the stress (dFc) and not forces. B13 is the controlled ablation inside our simulator: the objective, the render
  terms, the optimiser, the windows, u and the readout are the same, and only the control variable changes. Our prior
  F-control [Xu et al. 2025] is B4; the two blocks answer different questions (B4 the objective, B13 the control).
  *The arms (`--baseline force`, `--baseline force_mf`; without them the frozen path bit for bit).*
  - (a) `force`: an external force f_p(t) per particle and driven step, in the driven half of every window, the steps
    dFc acts in now. dFc is held at zero. The force enters as the particle's velocity increment c a_p before P2G, which
    spreads the impulse dt f_p to the nodes with the B-spline weights (and P2G's factor 1 − dt drag, which every
    momentum of the step takes). The leaf a is the force per unit mass in units of A0 = (λ + 2μ) V / (m dx), the
    acceleration that the P-wave modulus's unit stress gives one particle's volume V across one MPM cell; A0 = c_p² / dx
    with c_p the P-wave speed, the same at every N (bunny: c_p 13.5 wu/s, dx 0.306 wu, A0 ≈ 600 wu/s²); c = dt A0.
  - (b) `force_mf`: the same force, with each driven step's forces projected at that step's positions onto zero net
    force and zero net torque about the centre of mass: f' = f − a − b × r, a = mean f, b = I⁻¹ Σ r × f, I = Σ |r|² 1 −
    r rᵀ, r = x − x̄ (equal masses). The B-spline weights reproduce constants and linear functions, so the grid receives
    neither linear nor angular momentum from f'. This is the "momentum-free force" a reviewer would propose. It is
    still not the divergence of a stress: the force acts on each particle independently, and the projection is global.
  - Held equal: u as in our pipeline (its transport gate, its clamp, its rigid-mode removal, D146b's carried moments),
    so the comparison isolates dFc against the force; the layer relaxation (D146 `--relax_driven`), the minimum
    spacing, the bonds, the eight-term objective and the render terms (PCGrad, λ at the rule's value), Adam with the
    Armijo search, the per-particle per-step cap (0.02, here on |a|), the warm start (the last window's control × 0.5),
    the plastic assimilation at every commit (with dFc at zero it takes the elastic stretch the forces left), the
    acceptance and the stopping.
  - The step control's constants (Adam's eps, the adaptive step's target norm) are numbers in dFc's gradient units.
    They take the ratio of the physics gradient's norm on the force leaf to its norm on dFc, measured once at the run's
    first gradient (both at zero control), as D112 converted them to Xu's loss units; eps, a per-coordinate constant,
    takes that ratio × √3 (9 coordinates of dFc against 3 of the force per particle and step).
  - Not run: the Fattal–Lischinski driving force as a non-optimised reference. A faithful version needs its own target
    field, gathering term and per-scene gains, which is more than a few hours; the optimised arms are the stronger
    comparison.
  *Code paths (the design note).*
  - New: `physmorph/mpm/force.py`. It holds the increment and the projection kernels, with hand adjoints recorded on
    the tape. The projection's moments are summed in float64, and its adjoint includes the dependence on the positions.
  - `mpm/traj.py`: `Trajectory(force=...)`; in the driven steps P2G reads v + c f' in place of v.
  - `mpm/adjoints.record_p2g`: the velocity that P2G read (default `tr.v[t]`).
  - `mpm/function.py`: `RolloutSpec.force`, the force leaf of the persistent adjoint, and the bridge's fourth input.
    The bridge returns dFc's gradient only when dFc requires one; autograd discarded it before.
  - `pipeline/window/setup.py` (the unit, the eval trajectory's force buffer, `load`), `rollout.graph_terms`,
    `solve.py` (the leaf, the cap, the unit ratio, the record), `run/runner.py` (the `force_*` records),
    `TargetPack.force_ratio`, `config.py` (the baseline values, `force_scale`), `scripts/pipeline_run.py` (the choices,
    `--force_scale`; the Xu-only settings now keyed on "xu").
  - The default path: every change sits behind `cfg.baseline in (force, force_mf)` or `force is not None`; when off,
    P2G's inputs, the adjoint's arrays and every kernel are the old ones.
  - Records per committed window (`force_*`): the centre of mass's velocity increment the force gave (`force_dv`), the
    angular momentum per unit mass it added (`force_dL`), the gross increment, the leaf's largest entry, the unit ratio.
  *Tests (`tests/test_force_baseline.py`, on hyde06).*
  - (1) The projection has no net force and no net torque, and equals the float64 reference.
  - (2) The increment's hand adjoints, plain and projected, against float64 autograd of the same map.
  - (3) A window (persistent graphs, CPU and CUDA) against central finite differences on the force and u, both arms.
  - (4) Momentum: the grid's linear and angular momentum at every step. The plain force adds dt Σ f and dt Σ x × f; the

- **D146b, u's Adam moments carry from one window to the next (pre-registered 2026-10-14 02:15 CDT server clock, before
  any D146b run; the coordinator approved it as inside the framework: the optimiser's state of the existing u control).**
  *Read first.* (1) Kingma and Ba 2015 (Adam, ICLR), sec. 3: m and v start at zero, so their exponential averages are
  biased by (1 − β^t) and are divided by it; sec. 2.1: the effective step |Δ| ≤ α (1 − β1) / √(1 − β2) ≈ 3.2 α in the
  sparse case (a gradient after many zeros), α otherwise. (2) Diehl, Bock and Schlöder 2005 (the real-time iteration,
  SIAM J. Control Optim. 43): in a receding horizon the consecutive problems are nearly the same, and the solver's state
  of the last one (its iterate, shifted) is carried into the next instead of a cold restart; one iteration a sample then
  contracts. Our windows are such a sequence for u (the same particles' normal positions), whose solver state is now
  restarted. (3) Goh 2017 ("Why momentum really works", Distill): momentum averages the gradient over iterations and
  cancels the components that turn sign (the high-curvature directions) while steady ones accumulate; restarting it
  every window gives every window's first step at full size, which is the dither's mechanism. (4) Xiao et al. 2026
  (dynamic-sparse LLM training, arXiv 2606.00888): parameters regrown mid-run suffer a cold start under standard Adam,
  remedied by aligning the bias correction to each parameter's own age. *The change:* `config.u_adam_carry` /
  `--u_adam_carry` (an A/B switch, off = the frozen path): u's m and v carry from one committed window to the next; u
  itself still starts at zero every window (its last displacement is in the positions); dFc's moments stay per window
  (its warm start already carries its control); on an outer reject the carried moments go with the rejected lineage
  (cold restart, as the step memory and the warm start); a null window leaves them as they were. *The bias correction:*
  each coordinate counts its own age, the accepted iterations in which its gradient was nonzero (this one included), and
  divides m and v by 1 − β1^age and 1 − β2^age: a coordinate that starts to act (a particle entering the layer or u's
  gate) takes exactly Adam's first step g / (|g| + ε), as every coordinate does now at a window's first iteration; a
  carried one reads its averaged moments, so a coordinate whose gradient turns from one window to the next takes a small
  step and a steady one its full step. A count shared over the coordinates would misread a newcomer's age: too small a
  first step after a few iterations, up to 3.2× too large after many (source 1's sparse case); none is added. No new
  constant. *Tests* (`tests/test_u_adam_carry.py`, 4): the first step is Adam's and an idle coordinate stays (no NaN);
  a late starter gets the first step (the shared count's two errors shown); over two windows of eight iterations a
  turning coordinate moves < 0.35 × as far as with fresh moments and a steady one as far; in a run the moments reach the
  next window, stay fresh with the switch off and reset after an outer reject. *Runs* (`repo_d146c`: the code + the same
  hooks as D146a's, `d146_gate.sh`, the two-card cap, one dragon at a time): the main arm both switches
  (`--relax_driven --u_adam_carry`), 300k seed 97, bunny render arm and twin and dragon render arm and twin; then
  `--u_adam_carry` alone, bunny and dragon render arms, if the cards allow. *Gate:* D146a's items unchanged — (1) (a)
  the side view's late grey change ≤ 0.6 × the deliverable's, (b) the driven / other ratio ≤ 1.25, (c) the in-window
  excursion ≤ 0.5 × the baseline's, (d) the layer's reversal cosine above −0.3; (2) the 0–1.5 s bands; (3) the end,
  the relief and the roughness; (4) at rest; (5) the render lead; (6) no new visible piece; (7) cost — plus the
  coordinator's: (8) u's per-particle reversal slope (`d146_alt.py`) from −0.53 to ≥ −0.15, and (b)'s ratio below
  D146a's own. *Prediction:* u's slope −0.05 to −0.2; the layer's reversal −0.1 to −0.3; the driven-half layer path
  halves (the dither's share), so with D146a's calm release the late plateau falls to 0.4–0.55 × the deliverable's and

- **D147, the showcase scene: two thrown spheres collide, bounce apart, and each becomes its own bunny that lands and
  tumbles (design; opened 2026-10-14 01:00 CDT server clock; the coordinator's brief, the user's choice of two
  separate bodies over one merged bunny, and the user's clarification relayed at 01:20: "각각 따로 해야 할 거 같아. 두
  구가 bunny가 되어가며 충돌 해도 나중에 final은 bunny가 되어서 나뒹굴거나 해야 할 거 같은데"; the coordinator decides
  the routine choices and gives the go; the single-body path does not change, bit for bit; branch `wip/d147` holds the
  throwaway contact prototype, `scripts/probes/d147/contact_proto.py`, `output/gpu/d147/`).**
  *What the frozen pipeline lacks for it.* (1) Two bodies that touch and part: on one grid every node inside both
  kernels carries one velocity, so two bodies within two cells of each other move as one there and stick (Hu et al.
  2018: "the kernel support across the boundary naturally causes velocity field smoothing"; the prototype's
  single-field arm, P3). (2) An objective under which gravity, contact and spin may move a body: F1 stopped at G 0.1
  and under a sideways acceleration because the target, the cameras and the settling terms are fixed in the world
  and the selection merit rose as the centre of mass moved. (3) Time that always advances: the selection rejects a
  window whose merit rises by 5 % and restarts it from its start, and three rejections end the run; a collision or a
  landing raises the merit whatever the control does. (4) Two sources, two targets and a transport per body.
  *Measured before the design (M-a, read-only, `output/scratch/d147_buckens_drift.py` on D146's archive
  `d146/dragon300k_FT_frames12.npz`).* The material frame of an ordinary morph, R = polar(Σ (x − c)(X − X̄)ᵀ) with X
  the source sample: on the 300k dragon it turns 0.05° by 0.6 s, 0.84° by 1.8 s, 1.38° by 3.6 s and stays at
  1.50–1.53° to the end (14.3 s); the centre of mass moves 0.0000 wu; the frame's stretch S has eigenvalues 0.55,
  1.47, 2.03 at the end (well conditioned, far from the polar decomposition's degenerate case). The transport's flow
  is nearly irrotational (Brenier: the optimal map is a gradient, its Jacobian symmetric), so the material frame of
  a morph without spin stays within 1.5° of the world's: on the gallery a body-frame objective is a near no-op
  (checked by V0 below).
  *The contact prototype (M-b, pre-registered 02:00 CDT before any of its runs; `wip/d147`, `scripts/probes/d147/
  contact_proto.py`, `output/gpu/d147/`; queued for a free card through the lock directory, all four held by D145 and
  D146 at 01:30–02:00).* Two spheres of 20000 particles each (the stratified sampler, the shape's cell, E 1.4e5, ν
  0.2, the frozen F smoothing and the carried volume, drag 0, dt 1/240), 0.5 wu apart, no morph objective: P1 the
  gated rule head-on at v_rel / c = 0.1; P2 Bardenhagen's rule without the gate; P3 one field (the frozen grid); P4,
  P5 an impact offset of half a radius with μ = 0 and 0.5; P6 v_rel / c = 0.2; P8, P9 two spheres dropped 1 wu onto a
  floor (G 0.05) with the frozen grid floor and with the gated floor; P7 a taped window of 40 steps through the
  contact, the adjoint against central differences. Predictions: the interior node volume over the cell has a
  spread below 0.03 (the gate's noise); P1 bounces: at the first gated node the nearest cross-body particles are at
  most 1.5 spacings apart (touching), after the bounce no particle of either body lies within 1.5 spacings of the
  other, the total linear momentum stays at its start to 1e-5 relative and the angular momentum at zero; restitution
  between 0.3 and 0.8 (no prior: the bulk response is exact, the shear F smoothed). P2: the first contact at a
  surface gap of 2–4 cells (0.6–1.2 wu), the bodies turned back before they touch. P3: they stick (the relative
  velocity goes to zero and stays). P4 deflects with little spin, P5 spins both. P8 rests with its lowest particles
  1–2 cells above the floor, P9 within one spacing. P7: the tape within 5 % of the differences, or a mismatch the
  branch switches explain (measured, not a gate of the design).
  *Papers, contact (an agent's reading of the method sections; Huang et al. 2011 behind a login, read through Pan et
  al. 2008 of the same group and González Acosta et al. 2021, who adopted its normal; Lemiale et al. 2010 and Fei et al.
  2021 secondary).* Bardenhagen, Brackbill & Sulsky 2000: a nodal field per grain, the single-field velocity as the
  centre-of-mass velocity, "we define contact precisely when these fields differ"; approaching when (v_g − v_cm)·n_g >
  0, then v_g loses its normal part relative to v_cm ("allows grains to separate freely"), Coulomb by μ' = min(μ,
  |Δv × n| / Δv·n); a normal per grain, "which results in small errors in momentum conservation"; Pan et al. 2008:
  with it two colliding elastic spheres "move forward together" with strong dissipation. Bardenhagen et al. 2001:
  contact kept while the interpolated normal traction is compressive (releasing on departure "slightly increase[d]
  system energy"), and a velocity-change cap with a tuned α. Huang et al. 2011 / Pan et al. 2008 / Homel & Herbold
  2017: one normal for the pair, n₁ = −n₂ = (n₁ − n₂)/|n₁ − n₂| from the mass gradients, "for perfect conservation
  of linear momentum"; the projection p_r ← p_r − ((m_s p_r − m_r p_s)·n) n / (m_r + m_s) and the opposite change on
  p_s. Nairn 2003 (explicit cracks): the contact detected by the relative node volume V/V_cell, separated below 0.9,
  in contact above 1.1, the velocity test between ("stiffer materials … closer to one"); the velocity and traction
  tests alone found contact "long before visual evidence". Nairn 2013, Nairn, Bardenhagen & Smith 2018, Nairn et al.
  2020: approaching is "necessary, but not sufficient"; the gap δn = (x̄_b − x̄_a)·n̂ − 0.8h from the fields' mass-
  weighted positions, the 0.8 a fitted offset (0.92 GIMP, 0.96 CPDI by fit; errors up to 12 % at 5 % strain; every
  grid method detects early when the interface sits mid-cell); volume-gradient normals and their variants ("the best
  method depends on the problem"); one normal, since per-material normals broke momentum conservation. Liang et al.
  2024: false detection through shared nodes "is particularly prevalent" with B-splines; Han et al. 2019: the visible
  gap between elastic bodies is "proportionate to the Eulerian grid spacing"; Hu et al. 2018 (CPIC): one field
  "cannot represent discontinuous velocities", separation only across known rigid boundaries. Differentiable MPM:
  ChainQueen and DiffTaichi take the gradient of the branch taken (DiffTaichi: collisions "differentiable almost
  everywhere … similar to ReLU", saw-tooth gradients for rigid bodies without time-of-impact); PlasticineLab and
  SoftMAC smooth the contact by exp(−ζd) in the backward pass only (a sharpness constant; the hard-gradient arm
  optimised worse); BFEMP (IPC barrier, MPM–FEM, Newton); none with a field per body for two deformable bodies (the
  agent found no such paper). The gate chosen here is Nairn 2003's volume test with both thresholds at exactly one,
  which the partition of unity makes the touching condition (the agent derived the same: the first trigger of two
  touching spheres of 7.5 cells at about 0.09 h of overlap, 0.03 wu; the classical rule's first shared node at a
  surface gap of about 3.6 h, 1.1 wu); its weak point is noise in the node volume (measured in the prototype) and thin
  features below a cell (an ear 0.5 h thick needs about 0.3 h of overlap).
  *Papers, the body frame (an agent's reading of the method sections; not accessed: Canavin & Likins' journal paper,
  read through Canavin's 1976 dissertation it comes from, Shabana, Barbič & James 2005, Smith et al. 2019, read
  through Kim & Eberle's course notes).* Müller et al. 2005 (shape matching): with q = X − X̄ and p = x − c, the best
  linear map is A_pq A_qq⁻¹, A_qq symmetric ("only scaling but no rotation"), so the best rotation is the polar
  factor of A_pq = Σ m p qᵀ; the optimal translations are the two centres of mass; matching about the centres of mass
  with the masses as weights conserves linear and angular momentum. Canavin 1976 (the source of Canavin & Likins
  1977) defines the floating frames of a flexible body: principal axes (undefined for a sphere; Littlejohn & Reinsch
  1997: branch cuts and axis flips at degenerate shapes), Tisserand (zero relative angular momentum, H = Iω; a
  velocity constraint, so the frame is integrated in time and needs an initial orientation; Escapa 2014), and Buckens
  ("simply a first order Tisserand constraint", Σ m q × u = 0 with constant coefficients: holonomic, a function of
  the configuration). The Buckens condition is the stationarity condition of min_R Σ m |Rq − p|², so its frame is
  polar(A_pq) (also the Eckart frame of molecular physics, Kudin & Dymarsky 2005). Littlejohn & Reinsch 1997: the
  zero-angular-momentum frame is path dependent (its curvature does not vanish: the falling cat), and the kinetic
  energy splits into a purely rotational part and a frame-independent deformation part. Terzopoulos & Witkin 1988:
  x = c + R(r + e) about the centre of mass, the reference's rotation under its own Newton–Euler equations.
  Coros et al. 2012: controls on the rest shape are momentum conserving "as for muscles"; in mid-air a rest-shape
  change does not move the centre of mass; their objectives are in the world frame. Müller et al. 2007 (PBD damping)
  and Lu, Jin & Fedkiw 2016: the least-squares rigid velocity v_cm + ω × r with ω = I⁻¹L, removed "without
  influencing the global motion". DiffeoMorph (arXiv 2512.17129): a shape loss aligned by an inner optimisation over
  rotations; at the alignment's optimum the rotation can be detached (Danskin), the one case where a stop-gradient
  is exact; for a frame that does not minimise the loss itself it is not. The polar factor's derivative: for A = RS,
  dR = R[ω]× with ω = (tr S·I − S)⁻¹ vee(RᵀdA − dAᵀR) (McAdams et al. 2011, eq. 12; Twigg & Kačić-Alesić 2010;
  eigenvalues 2 / (σᵢ + σⱼ) on the twist directions, Kim & Eberle); it is finite whenever no two singular values sum
  to zero, also at S = sI, where torch's SVD backward divides by σᵢ² − σⱼ². The resulting position gradient,
  gᵢ = R[aᵢ − (mᵢ/M) Σaⱼ + mᵢ (κ × qᵢ)], κ = (tr S·I − S)⁻¹ Σ aⱼ × yⱼ, a = ∂ℓ/∂y, sums to zero and has no
  moment (Σ m y qᵀ = S): a self-equilibrated load, as the controls are. A stop-gradient frame leaves a net force and
  torque in the gradient that a control can only deliver through contact (Coros et al.: optimisers "automatically
  discover" contact propulsion): a biased gradient and a reason to exploit the collision.
  *Decisions (made by the agent with the papers above; the coordinator reviews).*
  (a) *Contact: one grid field per body, Bardenhagen's multi-velocity rule at the shared nodes, gated by the cell's
  volume.* P2G deposits each body into its own field (mass, momentum with the stress impulse, as MLS-MPM does); the
  grid operation computes each field's post-force velocity (gravity included); at a node where both fields have
  mass: the normal n = normalize(∇m₁ − ∇m₀) (the
  difference of the two fields' mass gradients, central differences of the node masses, the gradient of the grid's
  mass field; one normal shared by the pair, from body 0 into body 1, as Huang et al. 2011 and Homel & Herbold 2017),
  the bodies are in contact when their node volumes fill the cell, V₀ + V₁ ≥ dx³, and
  approaching, (v₀ − v_cm)·n > 0 with v_cm = (m₀v₀ + m₁v₁)/(m₀ + m₁) (on the post-force velocities, so
  compressed bodies whose stress pushes them apart are released by the same test, the concern of Bardenhagen 2001 and
  Pan et al. 2008); then body 0's velocity loses its normal part
  relative to v_cm, Δv₀ = −d n − min(1, μ d / |t|) t with d = (v₀ − v_cm)·n and t the tangential part of v₀ − v_cm
  (Coulomb), and body 1 takes −(m₀/m₁) Δv₀. G2P gathers each particle from its own field. The changes are equal and
  opposite at one node, so linear and angular momentum are conserved by construction. The gate: for two half-spaces
  touching at a plane, any partition-of-unity kernel gives V₀ + V₁ = dx³ at every node near the plane (Φ(a) + Φ(−a) =
  1, Φ the kernel's cumulative), less with a gap, more with an overlap; it is the touching condition itself, with no
  constant: Bardenhagen's rule without it acts as soon as both kernels reach a node, up to four cells apart for the
  cubic B-spline (the classical premature contact; prototype arm P2). Node volumes are the sample's volume per
  particle times the tracked J (`--volume_exact carried`), deposited outside the tape (they only decide the branch).
  The floor is the same rule with the floor as a body of infinite mass whose node volume is the kernel's part below
  it: in contact when V_b ≥ dx³ Φ((y_i − y_floor)/dx), so a body rests on the floor instead of on nodes up to two
  cells above it (the frozen code's grid floor; arm P8 against P9). Friction μ = 0.5 between the bodies and on the
  floor (a material constant of the scene, rubber on rubber, stated not tuned). Differentiable: the kernel is on the
  tape with Warp's generated adjoint; the gate and the approach test are branch conditions, constants of the adjoint
  (each step keeps its own gate volumes, since the generated adjoint replays the forward body); the normal is
  differentiated through the node masses. The jump at the switch is the usual non-smoothness of contact; spread
  over many nodes and steps it is smoothed in the aggregate, and the prototype's gradient check (P7) measures it.
  (b) *The single-body path stays bit for bit.* Each body is the frozen single-body Trajectory on its own particles
  (its stress, cell-ordered P2G with the hand adjoints, G2P, update, volume, bonds, minimum spacing and layer
  relaxation, every neighbour list local to the body, its own grid field on the shared world grid). The trajectory's
  step is split into three methods, before the grid, the grid operation, after the grid, which one body runs in the
  same order (code motion: the suite checks bit for bit); a new module steps two bodies: both parts before the grid,
  the pair's grid operation (the contact kernel, which also applies gravity, the walls and the floor to each field),
  both parts after it; its adjoint and torch bridge mirror the persistent adjoint (forward and adjoint as CUDA
  graphs), with the per-step positions as an extra output. The scene's optimiser is a subclass of the window
  optimiser; solve.py only gains the methods it overrides (the rollouts, the rigid modes of u, the commit), again code
  motion. Nothing of the scene runs unless the scene script is used.
  (c) *Each body's frame: the Buckens (shape-matching) frame.* c_b = the body's centroid, R_b = polar(A_b),
  A_b = Σ_p (x_p − c_b)(X_p − X̄_b)ᵀ, X the body's source sample at launch in its target's orientation. Every term of
  the body's objective (transport, surface proximity, end drift, near band, spray cleanup, silhouette, shading) is
  the frozen single-body term evaluated on y = R_bᵀ(x − c_b) against the body's own target in its canonical frame.
  R is differentiated exactly through a custom polar backward, Ā = R[κ]×, κ = (tr S·I − S)⁻¹ vee(RᵀḠ − ḠᵀR) for
  A = RS (finite for every A of rank ≥ 2, also the sphere's A ∝ I where the SVD's backward divides by zero); c by
  autograd. The objective is then invariant under each body's rigid motions and its position gradient has no rigid
  part (Σ∇ = 0, Σ r × ∇ = 0; a test). Not chosen: a Kabsch fit of the body to its target (undetermined while the body
  is a sphere and blind to a sphere's spin: the bunny would be formed in a frame that does not turn while the
  material spins, an internal circulation instead of a tumble); principal axes (degenerate for a sphere, flipping);
  the Tisserand frame, ω = I⁻¹L integrated in time (path dependent; the integral would have to be differentiated
  through the windows; equal to Buckens to first order in the deformation, M-a shows the deformation's part is
  1.5°).
  (d) *Velocity terms in the body frame.* The released motion and the end drift read v − (v_c + ω × r) per body and
  step, (v_c, ω) the mass-weighted least-squares rigid velocity (v_c the mean, ω = I⁻¹ Σ r × v): the deformation's
  kinetic energy (König), so a body that flies, spins or tumbles at rest pays nothing. The rollout's per-step
  positions become an output of the multi-body adjoint (seeds for x_t) for this; the single-body bridge is unchanged.
  (e) *Render: the cameras ride each body.* The 18 views and the target pictures of the frozen pipeline stay fixed in
  each body's canonical frame, which is the same as drawing the body at y: the views turn and travel with the body,
  each body is drawn alone, and the term keeps its resolution in pitches. Not chosen: one world camera set with
  per-body targets placed at the centres (not invariant to the tumble, sees one body occlude the other, changes
  resolution with distance). The deliverable video is a world view of both bodies and the floor (studio look; how
  the floor is drawn is open, below).
  (f) *Momentum budget.* The control dFc enters only the stress: Σ_i w_ip (x_i − x_p) = 0 cancels its net force, and
  the Kirchhoff stress P(F + dFc)ᵀ = P_e F_eᵀ is symmetric, so APIC keeps angular momentum (Jiang et al. 2015): a test,
  per body, with random controls, to float rounding. u and the relaxation are free of each body's six rigid
  displacement modes (per body: twelve modes, not six of the pair), so neither moves a centre of mass or turns a
  body's positions; they and the minimum spacing still change Σ r × m v, because they move positions without
  velocities (D99, D102: u +0.45 to +0.62 and the minimum spacing +0.27 to +0.55 of that injection at 300k; D101's
  projection failed its adjoint test). In a spinning body that injection scales with the spin; it is recorded per
  body and window and read against the contact's and the floor's torques, not fixed beforehand (measure first).
  (g) *Time always advances (the scene's acceptance).* The reference of a window in a dynamic scene is the
  uncontrolled continuation, not the previous window's merit: the line search already accepts a control only when it
  beats the window's start control (zero, or the warm start, itself kept only if it beats zero) on that window's own
  objective, collision included. So in the scene every window commits its line-searched control, or the zero
  control's rollout when no step was accepted or its replay failed; no outer rejection, no best-window truncation,
  the run lasts the scene's length. Invalid rollouts (non-finite, inverted, outside the domain) end the run.
  (h) *Material and forces.* Drag 0 (the existing `--drag 0`; M1: reached on all four meshes): the frozen 0.9 /s
  acts in the world frame and would take 83 % of a throw's speed in 2 s. Gravity by G = ρgH/E (F1's definition,
  g = 32.5 G wu/s²). The assimilation (D135) stays: an impact's elastic dent is half made plastic at the commit and
  the body-frame objective works it out; recorded as a risk. Restitution comes from the material: the volume is
  carried exactly (bulk response), the shear F is smoothed (s = 0.955), so the bounce is mainly volumetric; measured
  in the prototype.
  (i) *Two sources, two targets.* Each body is the canonical single body: its own stratified sphere sample of N_b
  particles (seed and seed + 50), mass 40000 / N_b a particle, its own density match, its own bunny sample (seed + 1
  and seed + 51, with their eight render draws), its own TargetPack, transport, ot_scale and unit ratios built in its
  canonical frame (the domain the single-body run would use; the loss grid follows N_b). One render weight λ for the
  sum (the bodies are alike). The bodies are contiguous index ranges [0, N_b), [N_b, 2N_b); every neighbour list
  (bonds, minimum spacing, the layer graph) and the fragment mask are per body. The world MPM grid: the shape's cell
  (diag / 26), a non-cubic box over the scene's reach plus the stencil margin.
  (j) *The scene's numbers (pre-registered from dimensionless groups, not tuned).* Impact speed v_rel / c = 0.1 (a
  rubber ball's regime; c = 13.4 wu/s, so v_rel = 1.34 wu/s, 0.67 each); gravity G = 0.05 (g = 1.62 wu/s²;
  between F1's 0.02 that held and 0.1 that failed in the world frame); the collision at t_c = 1.0 s (window 6, the
  bodies half-formed: D139's rise and the ears growing out at 0–1 s) at the apex (v_y = g t_c, rise 0.81 wu), the
  surfaces 1.34 wu apart at launch; the bottoms 1.0 wu above the floor at launch, landing at about 2.5 s; an oblique
  impact: the centres offset by half a radius vertically at contact, so that friction spins the bodies about the
  axis normal to the view (they land turning and tumble); each bunny's target turned to face the other at launch;
  8 s (48 windows). The 40k scene is two bodies of 40k (each as a gallery run); the 300k scene is 300k particles,
  two bodies of 150k (one 48 GB card holds a 300k run's 24–36 GB; two of 300k would not fit).
  *Evaluation (each body in its own frame; render arm and its render-off twin, seed 97; the 300k scene also seed 99).*
  E1 momentum: (i) a test, per body, controls on, no contact or gravity: linear and angular momentum unchanged to
  float rounding; (ii) in the scene, before the floor: the total linear momentum P₀ + M g t to 1e-4 relative, the
  total angular momentum about the pair's centre of mass and each body's budget (contact, floor, below-grid
  injection) per window. E2 ballistics: each centre of mass against its parabola until the first contact (internal
  forces cannot move it: to 1e-3 wu). E3 contact: the gap at the first gated node (cross-body nearest particles,
  in spacings; touching is about one spacing), the restitution and the spins after, no sticking (once the centres
  part, no particle of one body within 1.5 spacings of the other; no particle left behind on the other body), the
  interpenetration at the deepest point. E4 shape: per body at the end and over time, silhouette IoU, chamfer and
  thin uncovered in its frame against its target, against the 40k gallery's bunny (silhouette 0.975–0.978):
  reached = not more than 0.01 below. E5 floating pieces: the apart particles (d120_apart's measure) per body and
  window, and a frame-by-frame reading of the 4K frames around the collision and the landing (particle indices,
  [[frame-by-frame-particle-forensics]]). E6 render's influence: λ, g_share, the twin's E4 against the arm's.
  V0 (before the scene): one body, no gravity, no floor, the body-frame objective against the frozen world one, 40k
  bunny and dragon, seeds 97/99: inside the frozen code's run-to-run spread on silhouette, thin and chamfer.
  V1: one body thrown under G 0.05 and 0.1 onto the floor (F1's failing case): reached in its frame, at rest on the
  floor at the end.
  *Tests (pytest on hyde06, the exit status read).* The existing suite unchanged (the single-body path bit for bit);
  T-mom (per-body momentum under random controls; total momentum through a contact); T-sep (head-on bounce: the
  relative velocity reverses; the single-field control sticks); T-gate (two half-spaces: V₀ + V₁ = dx³ at the
  interface nodes within the sampling's noise); T-frame (y invariant under x → Qx + t; Σ∇ = 0 and Σ r × ∇ = 0; the
  polar backward against finite differences, A ∝ I included); T-rigid (a rigid motion has zero body-frame velocity);
  T-adj (the multi-body adjoint against finite differences through a contact); T-one (one body at R = I, c = 0: the
  scene objective equals the frozen one term by term).

  *How to use the contact code (a note for D148, 09:45 CDT).* `mpm/contact.py`: `k_grid_op_pair(gm0, gmom0, gvol0,
  gvel0, gm1, gmom1, gvol1, gvel1, dt, f_ext, gmin_y, dx, nx, ny, nz, floor_y, mu, impulse)` replaces `k_grid_op` for
  two grid fields on one grid (same dims, origin, dx): each field's post-force velocity mom / m + dt f_ext; at a node
  with both masses, the shared normal normalize(∇m1 − ∇m0) by central differences of the node masses, the gate
  gvol0 + gvol1 >= dx³, the approach test (v0 − v_cm)·n > 0, the normal part of the relative velocity removed and
  Coulomb mu on the tangential part, equal and opposite in momentum; then the domain walls and the gated floor per
  field (floor_y = −1e9: none); `impulse[0]` accumulates field 0's momentum change (a record, zero it yourself). It is
  launched on the tape and differentiated by Warp's generated adjoint (the gate and the approach test are branch
  conditions; the normal is differentiated through the node masses). `k_node_volume(x, J, vp, gvol, gmin, dx, inv_dx,
  nx, ny, nz)` deposits each particle's current volume vp·J (vp = the sample's fill volume / N: the interior then reads
  one) for the gate; launch it with `record_tape=False`, into a buffer per step on a tape (the generated adjoint of
  the pair's kernel replays the gate at backward time; a shared buffer would replay the last step's volumes).
  `k_grid_op_one` is the one-field version (walls, gated floor). `mpm/bodies.py`: `Bodies(trajs, vps, mu)` steps two
  Trajectory objects (each a body's own particles and arrays) on one prm: every `tr._pre_grid(t)` (stress, P2G into
  that trajectory's `gm[t]`, `gmom[t]`, with `adjoints.record_p2g` on a tape), the two `k_node_volume`, the pair's
  kernel, every `tr._post_grid(t)` (G2P with `record_g2p`, the update with `record_update`, the volume carry, the layer
  with `record_layer_project`); `BodiesAdjoint(specs, vps, mu)` is PersistentAdjoint for the pair (forward and adjoint
  as CUDA graphs, seeds for x_t, v_t of every step and F_T; `apply(dfc, u)` returns x_T, F_T, v_T, V, X concatenated in
  body order). The hand adjoints (`mpm/adjoints.py`: record_p2g, record_g2p, record_update, record_layer_project)
  take a Trajectory-like `tr` and a step t and read `tr.x[t]`, `tr.v[t]`, `tr.C[t]`, `tr.F[t]`, `tr.P[t]`, `tr.gm[t]`,
  `tr.gmom[t]`, `tr.gvel[t]`, `tr.v[t+1]`, `tr.C[t+1]`, `tr.Fraw[t+1]`, `tr.m`, `tr.vol`, `tr.prm`, `tr.device`,
  `tr.order`, `tr.order_blocks` (and the layer's and the bonds' arrays). For two particle groups of ONE body sharing
  one Trajectory, either (a) give the groups contiguous rows and pass the hand adjoints a view object whose per-step
  lists are Warp slices of the trajectory's arrays (Warp slices alias their parent's memory and gradient; checked on
  hyde06), with the cell order computed per group and every neighbour index the P2G reads (the fragment bonds'
  `bond_velocity`) local to the group's slice, or (b) add a per-particle field offset to P2G / G2P and their adjoints
  (`g + field[p] * ngrid` into fields stacked in one array; 0 everywhere reproduces the frozen path). (a) keeps the
  frozen kernels untouched, as D147 did by giving each body its own Trajectory. Measured (M-b, P1b): the gate's
  interior noise std 0.026 of the cell; it fires harmlessly at nodes where one side's kernel tail barely reaches;
  approach-only release gives no cohesion (two sides part freely once their post-force velocities separate); one field
  at v_rel/c 0.1 does not stick, it keeps a one-cell air gap and crushes the facing layers (J 0.74).

  rule leaves (it assimilates η = 0.5 a commit, so the rest decays 0.5, 0.25, …); in Fe_zero that leftover would never

  push, the weight, the floor) is not, so it stays elastic and the bounce and the stance survive; a load's elastic
  strain present at the window's start relaxes in the free rollout and is not assimilated either. For a body without

  **The four fixes and their 40k gate, pre-registered (2026-10-16 11:14 CDT server clock, before any of the gate's runs;
  the user's approval relayed by the coordinator ~11:00, "1–4 다 고쳐서 40k 확인"; scene code only, `wip/d147` fa0d091 +
  the gate's scripts, deployed `repo_d147fix`; `scripts/probes/d147/chain20.sh`, `output/gpu/d147/chain20.log`).**
  *The definitions as implemented.* (1) *Loss raster* (`scene/raster.py`): at each window start the window's persistent
  rollout is run with zero controls (the uncontrolled continuation), and each body's coordinates in its own frame are
  read over every step. The body's raster is the smallest cube that holds that extent with the preparation's own margin
  (two MPM cells, as prepare.py's "leash + 2 dx") inside the CIC deposit's last full cell. The cube is grown from the
  preparation's by whole steps (gcd of the MPM and loss cell counts: 9 MPM = 14 loss cells a side at 300k, one cell at
  40k), so the cell and every grid line are kept. The grown target is the frozen `build_target` on the grown cube, with
  the base target's unit ratios, transport scale and relief. A body inside the preparation's cube keeps its base target
  (the same object); grown targets are cached by step count. No new constant. (2) *Inf transport:* a body whose own
  geometry terms (transport with its end drift, stability, cleanup) are not finite at the window's start (the
  uncontrolled continuation) is left out of the window's objective. Its controls stay zero: its rows are zeroed in the
  gradient, the warm start and after every step. The other body is optimised as usual. If no body is finite, the sum
  is used as before. (3) *Replay mismatch* (commit_replay, commit_jt): as the single-body path treats a mismatched
  commit (a null window: no simulated time, the window solved again from the same start with the attempt's controls
  as its warm start), the scene's runner solves the window again, up to the single-body patience (5). Only after that
  is the zero-control continuation committed, recorded with `zero_reason`. Before, every such window committed the
  zero control as if it were the window's result. (4) *Damping* (`mpm/bodies.py`): each body's deformation velocity,
  v − (v_c + ω × r), is damped where the single-body drag acts (the velocity P2G reads, m v), at the single-body rate
  (MPMParams.drag, 0.9 / s, less the world's drag: 0.9 in the scene, none for V0). v_c and ω are the body's
  mass-weighted mean velocity and I⁻¹ Σ m r × v about its centre of mass (the particles' part; APIC's affine C is left,
  as the single-body drag leaves it). Σ m (v − v_c − ω × r) = 0 and Σ m r × (v − v_c − ω × r) = 0, so each body's
  P and L are kept; flight, spin and tumble are not damped. Warp kernels on the tape (generated adjoints), with P2G
  reading the damped velocities. `--drag 0` (no drag on the whole motion) stays. Records per window: `raster_k`,
  `raster_extent`, `inactive`, `zero_reason`, `replay_retries`; the scene info's `deformation_drag`.
  *Tests* (`tests/test_scene_fixes.py`): (4) the damping keeps P and L to rounding and scales only the deformation by
  1 − κ, leaves a rigid motion alone, keeps each body's P and L over a 48-step rollout of two spinning, deforming bodies
  while lowering their deformation energy below the undamped run's, is off under the world's drag, and the pair's
  adjoint with it matches central differences through a contact; (1) the grown raster keeps the cell and the grid
  lines (the 300k numbers: 5.28 wu kept at step 0, 7.06 wu needs one step), the grown target equals the base target on
  the base's cells and gives the same transport energy inside both, a state beyond the base raster is inf there and
  finite on the grown one, and the window's cover grows only the body that leaves (the other keeps its base object);
  (2) a body whose transport is inf is left out, keeps zero controls, and the other body's step is accepted and
  committed; (3) a mismatched replay returns a retry and no commit when allowed, the zero-control continuation with
  `zero_reason` when not; the runner solves a mismatched window again without simulated time; after the patience the
  continuation is committed and recorded. Then the full suite (the pinned digest included), exit status read; any
  failure stops the chain before a run.
  *The 40k gate (chain 20, one card idle for 10 minutes; the tests first on the same card).* Runs on
  `specs/scene_throw.json`, 2 × 40k, `--assim 0`, every 12th step kept: `fix40k_s97` (render arm), `fix40k_s97_off`
  (its render-off twin), `fix40k_s99`. References: `throwY40k_a`, `throwY40k_b` (the D135 recipe, the interim's, at
  40k on this spec and seed, 2026-10-14). Items, per run (`gate.py`; every run must pass items 1–4 and 6):
  (1) no zero-control window whose reason is one the fixes remove (nonfinite_loss, commit_replay or commit_jt after
  the patience); the other zero-control windows (no accepted step), the windows with a grown raster, a body left out,
  and the replay retries reported. (2) *Ears and head hold after the landing* (`head.py`; the forensic's
  head-displacement measure read the particles' rearrangement, not the shape, so the head is read as a shape): the
  head band is the top quarter of the target's height (the ears and the crown). At each kept frame, in the body's
  Buckens frame, the band's two-sided mean nearest distance between the target's points and the body's particles in
  the band, in sample spacings. Per body the recovery mean over [landing + 1.5 s, cut] must not exceed the larger of
  the two references' (same body); the recovery maximum and the 300k interim and final runs' values reported
  (context). (3) *Clean:* no piece apart from its body (apart.py, the whole run) of 10 particles or more beyond 3
  spacings before the cut (the user's "serious" size, 2026-10-15); the far frames reported. (4) *The judge*
  (judge.py): progress at the first contact in [0.35, 0.65], parted in the air, both landed, end error ≤ 0.05, early
  rise ≤ 3× steady. (5) The tumble reported. (6) *Momentum per body:* in flight before the first contact each body's P
  against P₀ + M g t within 1e-4 relative; over the first contact's windows the pair's P change less gravity's within
  1e-4 of body 0's launch momentum, and the pair's grid share of L less gravity's torque within 1e-4 of the bodies' L
  about the pair's centroid; in free flight between the parting and each landing, the body's grid share of its own L
  within 1e-3 of its spin. (7) The cost (minutes per run; the references 11.5).
  Pass → the 300k (s97, its twin, s99) is pre-registered and run; fail → stop and report.
  *Predictions:* (1) no fix-caused zero-control window; the raster grows in some windows after the landings (body 0
  from about 12.7 s), no body left out, a few replay retries, all resolved within the patience. (2) The heads hold at
  or below the references. (3) Clean of serious pieces. (4) All three pass; the collision and the floor bounce lose
  height to the damping (restitution below the 300k runs' 1.4–1.5; the pair still parts in the air before landing).
  (5) Smaller tumbles than 40k's 16–62°. (6) Within the bounds. (7) 12–13 min a run.
- **D148, the two sides of a target gap on their own grid fields (`--gap_split`; design opened 2026-10-14 09:36 CDT
  server clock; the user approved the direction, relayed by the coordinator: the crevice's foam at about 3.3–4.2 s and
  the two floating particles at about 5.1–5.4 s on the final dragon side video are to go physically; the deadline,
  relayed 10:30: everything including the gate's verdict today; the frozen single-body path stays bit for bit behind
  the switch, default off; `physmorph/mpm/gap_split.py`, `scripts/probes/d148/`, `output/gpu/d148/`).**
  *The cause (D137).* The shape's cell is about 6 pitches at 300k and the cubic kernel reaches 2 cells each way; every
  particle in a gap of the target narrower than about two cells (crevice 2.6–4.5 cells, neck and loop about 1.7) shares
  grid nodes with both rims, so one velocity field cannot carry the jump a split needs; the membrane stretches (J to
  1.3) and tears into beads. D137's proposal 2: the two sides on two fields, split by the transport's side labels.
  *Papers (an agent's reading of the full texts, 10:25 CDT; Wretborn et al. 2017 behind a paywall, read through Hu et al.
  2018).* Homel & Herbold 2017 (DFG): per particle–node pair, sgn(∇D_p · ∇D*_g) with ∇D*_g the gradient of the
  node's particle of largest damage gradient (the node's own gradient "fails when the grid node lies at the maximum of
  the scalar field"); field indices need not be consistent between nodes, only the normal at each node; the normal is
  the symmetrised mass gradient ½(n₁ − n₂); contact only when approaching, Coulomb; constants r_p, r_g, D_min (0.25),
  μ; a one-cell gap between contacting sides. Nairn 2003 / Guo & Nairn: per pair, the line from particle to node
  crossing an explicit crack (open ends need no rule); one geometric normal for both fields (exact momentum); the
  contact by the node volume, which "might be less than one even when the cracks are in contact" near free edges.
  Hu et al. 2018 (CPIC): node and particle colours from the sign of the distance to a known cutter, compatibility per
  pair, a geometric normal. Bardenhagen et al. 2000 / 2001: free separation, the approach test against v_cm, momentum
  exact only with equal and opposite normals. Moutsanidis et al. 2019: DFG with a threshold "to prevent spurious
  discontinuity detection". Nairn, Hammerquist & Smith 2020: a field's own gradient as the normal "not recommended"
  (momentum); for three or more materials at a node, each against all the others. No differentiable multi-field MPM
  was found.
  *Measured before the design (read-only, CPU; `scripts/probes/d148/d148_labels.py`, `d148_labels2.py` on FB's
  per-window dump `frozen_b/dump_dragon300k_FB`, windows 1–30 and every 10th, and its kept frames; `output/gpu/d148/
  labels_FB.{log,json}`, `labels2_FB.{log,json}`).* Gap nodes (definition below) on the dragon: 921 (90 of them with
  three or more pieces), in two large regions and six small ones; on the bunny 205 (13). For every particle in a gap
  node's reach and three candidate side rules, the side at that node against the side of the same plane its position
  at the run's end lies on (kernel-weighted): the debiased transport image x + (T_tgt − T_self) agrees 0.94 at 0.17 s,
  0.89–0.92 at 1–1.5 s, 0.94 at 2 s, 0.97 at 3 s, 0.98–0.99 at 3.7–5 s; the raw image T_tgt the same to 0.005; the
  particle's own position (CPIC's colour of a fixed medial plane) 0.59 at 0.17 s, 0.72 at 0.8 s, 0.89 at 1.5 s,
  0.95–0.98 later. The plane test agrees with the box's pieces (where the image's cell lies in one of them) 0.97. The
  sides flip 0.3–1.9 % of the pairs from one window to the next. Isolation, the debris mode (a particle alone on its
  side): at its heaviest split node, the only one of its side in that node's stencil: 0 or 1 particle a window
  (windows 1–30); every one of its links (1.5 pitches) on the other side: 2–30 particles a window. The reach: at window
  1 the split nodes (both sides present) are 337 and their stencils hold 220k of the 300k particles (the sphere covers
  both large regions); 616 nodes and 135k particles at 1.5 s, 750 nodes and 122k particles at 3–4 s.
  *Definition (the agent's decisions with the papers above; the coordinator reviews).*
  (1) *Gap nodes, from the target only, once a run.* The target's occupied cells at the loss cell (the cells holding at
  least one point of the target sample; at 300k 27 points a cell, no empty interior cell); a node outside the target
  (its own cell empty) whose kernel box |x − x_g|∞ < 2 dx holds two or more 26-connected pieces of them is a gap node.
  Its two sides are the two pieces with the largest kernel-weighted target mass in the box; its plane is the
  perpendicular bisector of their closest pair of target points (point m_g, unit normal n_g from side 0 to side 1: the
  medial plane where the gap is narrowest in the box). Everywhere else the single field exactly. No constant: the box
  is the kernel's reach, the cell the loss cell, the weights the kernel's. A node inside the target is never split:
  there the other rim is at least 1.7 cells away and its weight at most (0.3)³/6 per axis (0.005). A third piece at a
  node goes with the side of the plane it lies on (90 of 921 nodes; Nairn et al. 2020's lumping).
  (2) *Sides, per particle–node pair (the literature's form; no consistency between nodes needed, Homel & Herbold).* A
  particle's side at a gap node is the side of the node's plane its debiased transport image q_p = x_p + d_p lies on,
  d_p the label-free transport displacement the window start already computes for the u gate
  (`grid_transport_displacement` on the gate's grid, the shape's cell, blur one cell), frozen for the window like the
  u gate. Not chosen: the particle's position (CPIC's colour; it cuts material that must cross the medial plane:
  agreement 0.59 at 0.17 s); a damage-gradient partition (on a gap the medial surface is the ridge of the distance
  field, ∇D = 0 at its nodes: DFG's documented failure; and its r_p, r_g, D_min); one global label per particle
  (needs a 2-colouring of the walls across gaps); the box's pieces themselves for the image (0.97 the same; a table
  per node and cell in the kernels).
  (3) *The two fields at a split node: free separation, no slip while pressed.* With n = n_g: approaching,
  (v₀ − v₁)·n > 0, both fields take v_cm = (m₀v₀ + m₁v₁)/(m₀ + m₁), which is the single field's velocity at that node;
  separating, each keeps its own (Bardenhagen 2000's free separation). So a split node transmits compression and the
  shear that comes with it exactly as the single field does, and no tension: a no-tension interface on the gap's medial
  plane. No friction coefficient (μ would be an interface constant the body does not have; frictionless would make
  every medial plane a slip plane in a body that is still one material); the limit μ → ∞ of D147's rule. No volume
  gate: inside one body the gate reads the node volume's noise (std 0.026 of the cell, D147 P1b) as contact or not in
  the bulk, and Nairn 2003 notes the volume test fails at free edges, which a gap is; its purpose in D147, letting two
  bodies come within a cell before they interact, does not arise for two sides that only part. One geometric normal
  for both fields (Nairn 2003, CPIC): momentum exact at the node; the mass-gradient normal needs field identities
  consistent between nodes, which a per-pair partition does not have. Domain walls and floor as `k_grid_op` on each.
  (4) *Code (D147's second form, a field per particle and node, with the frozen transfers kept).* The frozen cell-ordered
  P2G deposits every particle into the total field as now; one extra per-particle kernel deposits each particle's
  side-1 part at split nodes into a second array (it returns at once for a particle with no gap node in its stencil);
  side 0 is the total minus side 1. The grid operation runs `k_grid_op`'s arithmetic at every node without a gap and the
  rule (3) at gap nodes with both sides; G2P gathers each particle's velocity and affine field from its side's field at
  gap nodes and from the total elsewhere (`k_g2p`'s arithmetic). Adjoint: the planes and the images are constants of
  the window (as the u gate and the bonds); the extra deposit and the grid operation by Warp's generated adjoints
  (the approach test replayed as D147's branches), G2P by a hand adjoint (`k_g2p_adj` with the side selection);
  tested against central differences. `--gap_split` (default off): off, no array, kernel or launch changes (the
  suite's bit-for-bit tests). The 40k path: the loss cell is the MPM cell there, so the 1.7-cell gaps may not resolve
  at 40k (the crevice does).

  *Papers on particles at a separation surface (an agent's reading, 13:50 CDT; full texts: Homel & Herbold 2017,
  Moutsanidis et al. 2019, Nairn 2003, Guo & Nairn 2006, Nairn, Hammerquist & Smith 2020, Hu et al. 2018, Wolper et
  al. 2019 and 2020; abstracts: Fei 2021, Daphalapurkar 2007, Sadeghirad 2011, Liang's XMPM, Kakouris & Triantafyllou
  2019, Fei & Choo 2020).* What keeps them free of debris at a crack's start: one side per particle, the same at every
  node (Nairn's one global crack: the line from particle to node crosses it or not; Homel's particle gradient, the same
  at every node; CPIC's one tag per particle and surface); the side persistent (CPIC: "will persist after being
  obtained, until all nodes in p's kernel lose affinities"; Nairn's crack particles move with the material); ambiguity
  read as connected (Moutsanidis's threshold, CPIC's distance-weighted vote); the split only once the material there
  has failed or thinned (Homel's min(D̄1, D̄2) > D_min: "the material should be allowed to separate only once a
  'surface' of failure particles has formed"; Nairn's relative volume). No MPM scheme found splits a particle's mass
  between two velocity fields. Homel names our saddle: the partition "fails when the grid node lies at the maximum of
  the scalar field ... quite frequently at the border of a fully damaged region". And a defect of D148's own
  definition the reading exposes: each gap node's plane is its own closest pair's, so neighbouring nodes' planes differ
  in place and orientation, and a particle near them is side 1 at one node and side 0 at the next. The forensic shows
  exactly that: the beads' particles were on side 1 at 0.51–0.88 of their nodes (GA's opening bead 0.51–0.65 at
  0–1.5 s, its upper-hole bead 0.71–0.78), so both fields pulled on them.
  *The candidates against the two failures (the coin-toss sides within a blur of the cut, mixed between nodes; the
  opening at 1.3–1.6 s instead of 3.3 s).* (a) Soft sides (the share of side 1 the plan's mass beyond the plane under
  its blur; `--gap_split soft`, built): a particle with a share near one half moves with the mean of the two faces'
  velocities, so as they part it stays at mid-gap: a bead by construction (the reading's inference too), and the band
  of mixed particles is one blur wide, the width of the gap itself; no effect on the opening. (b) Sides by position
  against the medial planes (CPIC, Nairn): wrong while material must still cross the target's plane (agreement 0.59 at
  0.17 s, measured), so an earlier and wronger split; needs CPIC's persistence and penalty constant. (c) Variant B (the
  split only where the node's particle volume is below one cell) with the transport sides: delays the opening (the
  bulk never splits; its noise splits about half the bulk's gap nodes); leaves the coin toss and the mixed sides. (d)
  Persistent sides alone: stops the flipping, not the first coin toss, not the mixed sides between nodes, not the
  opening. (e) One wall per particle and gap region, persistent, gated: the walls of each gap region labelled once a
  run and consistently across its nodes (each gap node's two pieces joined with its neighbours' through their shared
  occupied cells, a breadth-first pass over the region; a piece meeting both labels makes its node single-field); a
  particle's side in a region the wall whose occupied cell holds its transport image, kept from the window before
  while the image lies in the gap's empty cells (no constant: occupancy is the loss cell's); the field index at every
  node of the region that particle's one side, the node's normal oriented from wall 0 to wall 1; with B's gate
  (Homel's "surface of failure"). The best by the reading and by the forensic: it removes the mixed sides between
  nodes (the beads' mechanism), freezes the saddle's coin toss (the stranded ones), and the gate delays the opening.
  D148b (finer sides) narrows the coin toss's band but keeps the mixed sides between nodes.

  **D148d proposed (16:00 CDT, not built, not run):** at a node whose box does not hold the particle's representative
  cell, the side is the node's piece nearest to that cell (the piece of the box's occupied cell nearest to it) in place
  of the plane; the plane only where the nearest is a third piece. A wall is continuous, so the wall holding the kept
  cell continues into the neighbouring box, and the wall across the gap lies at least the gap farther. Implementation: a
  nearest-occupied-piece map per gap node over its box, read at the representative cell clamped into the box; the hand
  adjoints unchanged (the sides are constants). The check before any run on the CPU: the plane-decided mass to about
  zero on WG's and FB's states, the opening beads' sides consistent at all their nodes, and the nearest wall the one
  each bead ends on. Then a 300k pair on D146b with `--term_dump` (windows 6–22) for the beads with consistent sides.
  The early opening itself (the divergence released) is not a gate item ((2) passes) and is left as it is.

  cell keeps its own), the kernels' `side_share(..., clampk = 1)` read a representative cell outside the box at the box
  cell closest to it; the plane only where that piece is a third one; B's gate as walls. Tests added (CPU): (17) the map

  ratio L(t)/L(0); α = 0 pins the gradient norms (ours is that rule with a ratio of 0.5), α > 0 moves weight to
  the task whose ratio is higher in proportion to its ratio^α. FAMO (Liu et al. 2023): balanced descent is an
  equal relative improvement (ℓ_t − ℓ_t+1) / ℓ_t of every loss, the direction Σ z_i ∇ℓ_i / ℓ_i, the weights adapted
  from the observed log-loss decreases with a rate β and a decay γ; integrating its update with β = 1, γ = 0
  gives weights in proportion to the loss ratios, i.e. the objective Σ L_i / L_i(0), a weight held at the
  source's values (the family D73 measured), and its equal-weight direction is the sum of the log losses (λ = P /
  R). DWA (Liu, Johns and Davison 2019): weights from the last two epochs' loss ratios through a temperature T (a
  constant). Nash-MTL (Navon et al. 2022): maximise Σ log(g_i · d), GᵀGα = 1/α, invariant to loss scaling; for
  orthogonal gradients α_i = 1 / |g_i|, equal norms, close to the present rule. MGDA (Sener and Koltun 2018): the
  min-norm point of the gradients' hull, a common descent direction, on raw gradients. What these give here: every
  "equal rate" rule moves weight to the term whose relative loss falls slower, which is the render after the

  D102's split at 300k: of the angular momentum the updates below the grid put in, u carries +0.45 to +0.62, the
  minimum spacing +0.27 to +0.55, the relaxation ≈ 0. The definition tried: at every step the layer's normal
  displacement s n (u and the relaxation together) loses its part along nine modes, the six rigid ones (n, r × n;
  static, D98's inverse) and the three along which it puts angular momentum in (q = n × v, the displacement
  carrying the particle's momentum: Σ s n × v = Σ s q), the 9 × 9 Gram system solved per step on the tape by the
  Schur complement of the static block (`k_layer_relax` moments, a one-thread `k_layer_solve`, `k_layer_project`).
  A new test (a turning slab: every step's displacement free of translation, rotation and injection to 1e-3) passed;
  the adjoint against finite differences with the layer on (`test_adjoint_matches_finite_differences_with_force`)
  failed, −0.0527 against −0.0333 (D98's kernels pass it). The cause is in the definition: q scales with the
  velocity, so the Schur block S ~ |v|² and the coefficient ~ s / |v|; near rest (the test's first steps, every
  run's late windows) the projection's direction is set by the velocity's noise and its derivative grows as
  1 / |v|². Damping it needs a velocity scale, a new constant. Reverted (the kernels are D98's); the angular
  momentum the jumps put in is left as it is, the render arm already holding less of it than its twin (D102).
  user, on D100's late trade of the silhouette: "2번도 확인 해 줘"; and on D102: the conservation measure is the
  angular momentum, "각운동량이라고 해도 좋아"; code: `run/selection.py` best_window).** The delivered slice ends at
  the best window by the selection merit, every window scored at one render weight; that weight is the last
  window's, which follows the physics gradient down (D81), so late windows that give up silhouette for transport
  score as better (D100: the delivered silhouette term 1.2 to 2.7 times its run minimum on half the gallery).
  The definition: windows are compared at the largest render weight of the epoch, the weight at which the run
  valued its pictures most; the merit stays linear in it, nothing else changes (the optimisation, the stop and
  the physics-only twin, whose weight is zero, are as before). Evaluation: the choice is made after the run on
  its records, so it is evaluated exactly on runs already made: the D98 pair's render arms (bunny, dragon 300k;
  display against the independent sample from their kept frames' readings: the last 20 kept frames up to the
  new end), D102's render arms (records: kinetic energy, angular momentum at the new end), the D100 gallery's D
  arms (the run's own silhouette term and transport at the chosen window). Criteria: the delivered silhouette
  term at most 1.05 times the run minimum in median (now 1.12) and above 1.2 on at most 2 of 19 meshes (now 8);
  at 300k the display against the independent sample at the new end not worse than at the old (last 20 frames)

  2026-10-04 16:17 CDT at launch of the first run; the user: "A, B 둘다 봐야", "Render gradient가 유의미한 결과를
  낼 때까지 계속 진행"; code: `window/solve.py`; servers `repo_r69` (D77, this change alone) and `repo_r70`
  (D78, with D74's pictures); `output/gpu/d77`, `output/gpu/d78`; `tmp/d77.sh`).** D73's first cause: the
  weight λ is set once so that λ|g_render| = 0.5 |g_phys|, and held; the physics gradient then decays 30-fold
  and the render gradient 1.4-fold, and from window 10 on the step is 91–96 % render. The change: the same
  rule with the same constant holds at every gradient as a bound on the step, the render gradient enters at
  min(λ, 0.5 |g_phys| / |g_render|), so its share of the step is at most a third. The merit does not change: E
  = L_phys + λ L_render with the one λ is what the line search and the outer acceptance compare, and the line
  search's slope is taken on E's own gradient. Five lines; no new constant. This is not the earlier balancer
  (which moved the merit's own weight every iteration and was a source of oscillation): the function being
  minimised stays one function.
  Primary sources (one agent, received 16:10 CDT; method and theory sections read from the arXiv sources, not
  cover to cover; Désidéri 2012 only through Sener and Koltun): PCGrad (Yu 2020) acts only on a negative
  cosine, "the original gradient remains unaltered" otherwise, and names the regime here, a dominating
  gradient whose improvement "may be significantly overestimated". Rules driven by loss ratios (GradNorm,
  Chen 2018) put "more weight on tasks whose losses are dropping more slowly", which is the term at its floor.
  MGDA's min-norm point (Sener and Koltun 2018) takes the physics gradient alone whenever the cosine exceeds
  the ratio of the norms (0.05 here), dropping the render from the step. The rules that bound an auxiliary
  gradient by the main one's norm are MetaBalance (He 2022: the auxiliary gradient is scaled to the target's
  norm when it exceeds it), MTAdam (Malkiel and Wolf 2020, anchored on the first term) and the gradient-
  statistics weights of physics-informed networks (Wang, Teng and Perdikaris 2021), none with a line search
  on a fixed merit. For that part: a direction d = −(g_p + β g_r) is a descent direction of E for any β ≥ 0
  when the cosine of the two gradients is not negative, which the projection guarantees, and backtracking on
  a descent direction keeps Zoutendijk's condition (Nocedal and Wright, Thm 3.2); through Adam's diagonal
  scaling that is not automatic, so the slope is computed on E's gradient as the code already does. Reported
  cautions: equalising norms lifts a noisy gradient to parity (MetaBalance: exact equality "might not be
  optimal for the target task"); Kurin 2022 and Xin 2022 find such methods land on the scalarisation front,
  the question being which weight, not which method.

  1. The weight is set once, at the first window (at window 2 the two gradients are equal, share 0.51). The

  The cosine between the two is +0.1 to +0.25: they do not oppose each other, one is simply larger.
  2. The physics objective is starved of the step: its gain per window is 6 times smaller than the twin's at
  window 20, 100 times at window 30, 2 to 7 times after; the transport energy is 2 to 8 times the twin's at the
  same window and 8 times at the end. The same without the rule (D64's run against D60's: share 0.90–0.93,
  transport 3 to 5 times the twin's at windows 20–60), so this is not the rule's doing. Until window 10 the
  render arm is ahead on everything (crop 0.931 against 0.831): while the body is far from its target the
  coarse picture is a good guide.
  3. What that share buys after window 20: the run's own 64-px silhouette term 3 times below the twin's (3.7e-4
  against 1.1e-3 at window 40), and on the 96-px yardstick an exterior silhouette that is not lower but higher
  than the twin's from window 30 to the end of the stage (1.9e-3 against 1.5e-3, 1.4e-3 against 1.3e-3, 1.23e-3
  against 1.05e-3). A 64-px pixel is 3.8 pitches on the dragon: the term is fitted at its own resolution in a
  way that does not hold one resolution finer, and the horn crop is behind from window 20. The fine stage,
  whose picture does see the difference (5.7e-4 at window 80), comes at animation 79–84 and lasts 11–22
  windows.
  4. Bunny 300k, the same composition (share 0.95, transport 4 to 5 times the twin's), but there the 64-px fit
  carries over: the yardstick is 1.35 times below the twin's at window 20 (9.3e-4 against 1.26e-3) and twice
  below once the fine stage runs (4.3e-4 against 8.7e-4 at window 40); the IoU is ahead.
  5. 40k (D72's dragon, both arms with the rule), the same share (0.82–0.92) and two to three times the twin's
  transport energy; there the twin's own 64-px silhouette term stalls at 3.1e-3 to 4.5e-3 with a physics gain
  near zero from window 40 (+0.006, −0.010) and 13 % of the thin target uncovered, an error a 64-px picture
  sees (a pixel is 1.9 pitches at 40k), and the render arm removes it (9.8e-4 at window 20): silhouette IoU
  +0.009 to +0.013 on the six meshes read so far.
  Conclusion: at 300k the render arm is behind for two reasons that act together. Its weight is fixed at the
  first window while the physics gradient decays, so after window 10 the step is a render step and the physics
  objective gets a few per cent of it. And at 300k that step is taken on a picture whose pixel is 3 to 4
  pitches, in which the physics-only arm (which with the rule already stands at the floor on the dragon's
  crop) has no error left to see; the stage whose picture is fine enough comes late and is short. At 40k the
  second reason is reversed: the picture is finer against the particles and the physics-only arm leaves more.
  Not measured: whether a bounded share, or a fine picture from the window where the coarse term stops
  falling, would put the 300k render arm ahead. Those are two definitions (the weight's calibration, the
  stage's trigger), one experiment each.

- **D70, a minimum spacing in the position update (pre-registered 2026-10-04 11:55 CDT; the user: "A를 진행 해
  보자", "원인을 감추지만 말아 줘. overengineering도 금지 … 항상 '알고리즘' core를 수정", "'항상' 랜더 Gradient가
  영향을 끼치는지 확인"; code: `kernels.k_update`, `--min_spacing 0.9`; server `repo_r66`; `output/gpu/d70`).**
  The cause (D66–D69): the grid holds about 200 particles a cell and cannot see two of them pressed together;
  where the material is stretched and torn the density under the surface ends uneven, and the drawn surface
  with it. The position update already holds the two rules that act below the grid (the bonds' re-joining and
  the outer layer's relaxation), and its comment left compression to the grid. One rule is added there: a
  particle is moved away from each of its 16 nearest (frozen at the window's start) that is nearer than r, by
  half the overlap, over one window (the bonds' fraction per step); r is 0.9 of the pitch the rest volume
  gives, the spacing of a Poisson-disk sample of the body's density (random sequential packing stops at a
  packing fraction of 0.38). Twelve lines in the kernel, the neighbour rows in the window's setup; no surface
  rule, no kernel sums. On kept frames (D69) ten such projections brought the band below 4 pitches to a
  sample's level on the bunny and removed half of its excess on the dragon, a quarter to two fifths of the
  4–11 band's, with no material leaving the surface; the body's surface moved out by 0.006–0.01 pitches a
  projection, which in a run the objective has to hold.
  Runs, 300k, bunny and dragon, each with the minimum spacing: the physics-only twin (kept, as D60's) and the
  render on the exterior at 192 px (D64's setting); against D60's and D64's runs without it. Read on every kept
  frame: the surface's offset from the mesh by band and the normals (D66's probe), the density's spread and the
  nearest particle under the surface, the display against the target and against D65's floor, the render terms
  on the yardstick, and the render's effect under the new rule (with-render against its own physics-only twin,
  as D62).
  Criteria: under the surface the density's spread and the nearest particle's 5th percentile at a sample's
  level (0.21; 0.36 pitches) at the end; the band below 4 pitches within 5 % of a sample's and the 4–11 band's
  excess at most half of what it is without the rule (bunny 0.039–0.045, dragon 0.075–0.104); the display's
  difference against the target a third of the way from the present runs to the floor or better (bunny front
  0.0096 → 0.0085, dragon 0.0127 → 0.0109), with no solid region's IoU lower than without the rule by more than
  the runs' spread (0.0008); the body not further out (mean offset within 0.05 pitches of the run without the
  rule); the transport energy and the run's length within a quarter of the run without it; the render's effect
  on its own terms kept (silhouette at least twice below the twin's at the end).
  Expectation: the fine band reaches a sample's; the 4–11 band's excess falls by a third to a half; the
  pictures' difference by a fifth to a third of the gap; a window costs under 5 % more. Risks: thin sheets
  fatten (a sheet one or two particles thick is pushed to r), the body swells where clumps were, the transport
  slows because the projection works against a control that presses material together.
  Primary sources (one agent; received 12:06 CDT, after the runs were started; five of ten papers read in full,
  the others through their authors' theses or later papers, as marked in its report): the rule is of the kind
  hybrid particle-grid methods use, Ando and Tsuruno 2011 (Eq. 7) and Ando, Thuerey and Tsuruno 2012 (Eq. 18):
  every step a particle is pushed away from each neighbour within a distance d, along the unit vector, weighted
  1 − r²/d², with no rule for the free surface; they re-sample the velocity afterwards and name the fault of
  the isotropic form, it "can lead to a thickening of thin surfaces, or a smearing out of sharp features". In
  MPM, Baumgarten and Kamrin 2023 shift material points and leave "material and state properties unchanged",
  as here (F, C and the velocity are not touched); their grid-based correction is a node quantity and cannot
  order particles below a cell, and of the rules they compare the neighbour-based one of Xu, Stansby and
  Laurence 2009 (δr = C α Σ (r̄²/r²) n over a fixed list of neighbours) gave the evenest arrangement. The
  concentration-gradient shifting of SPH (Lind 2012, Khayyer 2017, Sun 2017–2019) needs a free-surface rule
  (tangential projection, eigenvalue thresholds, a step limit) to keep the surface in place, which is what
  D69's first candidate lacked. What differs here from Ando's form: the push is the overlap below r (zero
  beyond it), not a kernel of the distance, so a pair at r or farther is left alone.
  **Result (2026-10-04 13:27 CDT; the four runs to their own stop; every reading on all kept frames, the tables
  the mean of the last 20; `output/gpu/d70`: `t_`, `a_`, `o_`, `e_`, `f_` logs, `twin_{bunny,dragon}300k.png`,
  local `output/video_2026-10-04/d70_min_spacing/`).** P and L192 are D60's and D64's runs without the rule, PA
  and LA the same two with it.

- **D61, the exterior's field: Solenthaler's factor on the offset (stage 1c; display only; pre-registered
  2026-10-03 23:33 CDT; the user: "OK. 들어가 줘" to the field first, then stages 2 and 3; code
  `physmorph/render/exterior.py`, `surface_layer_probe.py … FIELD`).** D59's webs between the ears, sheets in
  concavities and bridged sparse particles are one fault: between near but separate bodies the particles' mean
  x̄(q) moves faster than q and |q − x̄| stays below the offset where there is no body.
  Primary sources (one agent, the papers' own text; copies in the session's scratch directory): Zhu and Bridson
  2005 name the fault ("spurious blobs of surface can appear, since x̄ may erroneously end up outside the surface
  in concavities") and smooth it away on a grid; Solenthaler, Schläfli and Pajarola 2007 (Eq. 23–26) remove it at
  its cause, "in concave regions or between near but separated particles", by multiplying the offset with
  f = γ³ − 3γ² + 3γ, γ = (t_high − EV_max)/(t_high − t_low), EV_max the largest eigenvalue of ∂x̄/∂q, t_low 0.4,
  t_high 2.0 (f = 1 below t_low; 0 above t_high, implied); Yu and Turk 2013 (anisotropic kernels) address
  bumpiness, make no claim on gaps, and their centre smoothing itself pulls components within four spacings
  together (they add component labels against it); Adams 2007 needs distances carried from step to step;
  Bhattacharya 2015 has "difficulty generating very thin surfaces". So the change is Solenthaler's factor with
  the paper's constants on the field as it is (kernel radius 3 pitches); the eigenvalue is the largest real part,
  from the characteristic cubic in closed form; the offset is set once more so that the target samples keep the
  base display's solid area (the factor is about 0.947 on a flat surface, so 0.845 pitches first, then corrected
  by the measured ratio).

  build), each against its `zb` rows.
